assessment_summary: I validated the installation against the guide's documented Linux method (clone repo, ensure Docker running, run `make run`). 1) Repository: /workspace contains the SmartPlanAI repo at commit 1d70807 with the exact artifacts the guide references (Makefile 'run' target invoking docker compose up --build, deployment/docker-compose.yml, windows_run.cmd, Dockerfile), matching the summary. 2) Prerequisites: Docker Engine 29.7.2 and Compose plugin are running, so the documented prerequisite holds. 3) Execution evidence: /workspace/make_run.log shows the documented `make run` command completed the multi-stage build (image blp-streamlit-pipeline:latest named, 'Image … Built', container created and started), and make_run.log is the only untracked file (no abandoned alternate methods). 4) Runtime behavior: independent HTTP checks from the host against localhost:8501 returned 200 for the Streamlit root page and 200 'ok' for /_stcore/health; the container log shows Streamlit's normal startup message and zero traceback/error/exception lines. 5) Image integrity: inside the container I confirmed the app code is present and its modules import (src.utils.session_state imports cleanly), streamlit 1.55.0 and paddle 3.2.2 are installed, PaddleOCR model files exist under /home/appuser/.paddlex, and ffmpeg/pdftoppm (documented runtime tools) are available. 6) Known caveat: docker ps reports '(unhealthy)'; I traced this to the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK 'curl --fail http://localhost:8501/_stcore/health' while the runtime image has no curl binary (healthcheck exit 127, 'curl: not found'). The app itself answers both endpoints correctly, so this is a defect in the upstream image's healthcheck command, not an installation or operational failure; fixing it would require rebuilding the image, which is outside validation boundaries and unnecessary for the app to operate. Limitations: I did not perform an end-to-end digitization (upload a building plan and produce XPlan.gml) since that requires sample input data and interactive browser use; however, the guide's success criteria are that `make run` starts the application via Docker, which is verified by the running container and live HTTP responses. Based on the complete, running installation and the application responding on its documented interface, the outcome is assessed as success.
